值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析《BLEACH 死神》藍染惣右介與《咒術迴戰》兩面宿儺在動漫迷心中評價兩極化的關鍵成因。
  • 詳細解析優秀反派塑造的必備特質，說明為何初期的宿儺具備王者風範，後期卻淪為讀者嘲諷的對象。
  • 探討《咒術迴戰》後期戰鬥邏輯與「束縛」設定的崩壞，如何直接摧毀反派首領的威嚴與作品深度。

摘要

宿儺與藍染的相似起點：從容霸氣的王者風範

作者井川一指出，《咒術迴戰》在創作上深受《BLEACH 死神》的深遠影響，而作品中的兩大核心反派藍染惣右介與兩面宿儺在連載初期有著極高的共通點。兩者皆具備傲視一切的狂妄性格、強大無匹的戰鬥力，身邊亦各配置了兩名隨從。在澀谷事變中，宿儺面對特級咒靈漏瑚時游刃有餘，甚至在擊敗對手後給予由衷讚賞，展現出強者兼具原則與格調的魔王風範，與藍染當年隻手壓制護廷十三隊的強大壓迫感如出一轍。

藍染的立體魅力：智謀與實力的多重幻術

作者進一步探討，藍染之所以能成為 Jump 史上最令人敬佩的反派之一，在於他的威脅性不僅來自斬魄刀鏡花水月的絕對催眠，更來自他深沉的心計與人性操弄。透過過去戲耍平子真子的經典橋段，藍染證明了自身的智謀始終凌駕於眾人之上。相較於僅靠作者旁白單方面強調「實力尚未用盡」，藍染這種將計謀、性格與能力完美融合的表現，才真正構建出一個令人信服且深具層次的高智商反派。

宿儺評價崩壞的根源：戰鬥機制的濫用與人設崩塌

然而，宿儺在後期與五條悟的宿命決戰中，反派格調徹底崩盤。作者分析指出，宿儺本身斬擊術式單一，在無法突破無下限術式的情況下過度仰賴魔虛羅，喪失了身為頂點強者的從容；更嚴重的是，作者過度濫用束縛機制，使原本精巧的「等價交換」淪為推進劇情的便利工具，甚至以極其微小的代價換取逆轉戰局的空間斬。這類失衡的劇情邏輯暴露出能力體系過度膨脹卻無法圓滿自洽的問題，最終讓宿儺在讀者眼中淪為被劇情強行偏袒的笑柄。

================================================

When you hear the. name Aizen, what’s the first thing. that comes to mind? That's right,. illusions and his revolt within the. Soul Society. These represent the sheer. strength that Aizen possesses, leaving. a deep impression on the audience. Personally, my favorite part has always. been how he cleverly tricked Shinji in. the past, making him think, "Oh, I've. already figured out your trail.""Too. bad, little did he know those clues. were actually provided to him by yours.

truly!" It was precisely because Shinji. was so guarded against Aizen and kept. him at a distance that he ended up. being fooled by the simplest of tricks. In reality, the person who had been. following him for the past few weeks. was just a random passerby, and he. didn't even notice. This scene shows us. that Aizen's illusions aren't just. limited to his Zanpakuto's abilities,. but are actually multifaceted,. incorporating his own character and. schemes—all of which are part of his. trickery. To me, this is a much more. effective way to depict a boss than. constantly hyping up how strong they. are or claiming they haven't even used. their full power yet. You know what I. mean? There are. many theories as to why Sukuna's. performance in the later stages was so. pathetic. Some say it's because. Sukuna’s base technique is just too. weak—he just slices things up. Against Gojo's Infinity, he couldn't. even shave the guy’s leg hair,. leaving him dependent on Mahoraga to. adapt for him. He's a total fraud. Others say it's because the "Binding. Vow" mechanic was completely abused. It. was supposed to be a genius patch Gege. came up with to fix the "exposition. disease" trope. In Bleach, characters. act like idiots by explaining their. trump cards to enemies, causing them to. lose; in Jujutsu, doing that actually. benefits you, giving yourself a buff—. wow, how creative. But later on, this. Binding Vow gradually evolved from a. cool "equivalent exchange" into a "get. out of jail free" card that the author. forces into the plot to explain why. things turned out this way. Whenever a. plot development feels unreasonable, he. just says, "It’s a Binding Vow, I. used a Binding Vow." The most notorious. example is undoubtedly when Sukuna. needed to instant-cast the. It's. about the same concept as me trading. you a bottle cap for the one million. dollars in your hand. Both of the. aforementioned deductions are correct,. but ultimately, I still think it comes. down to the author himself. He made the. manga's ability system unnecessarily. complicated, but didn't have the energy. or skill to organize the logic clearly,. which is why the finished product had. so many issues in the later stages of. Bleach. If you ask me, I have the exact. same problem, especially with Yhwach's. "The Almighty." Honestly, and I say. this with a clear conscience, I think. the level of nonsense is on par with " Dragon's Claw" or "Flowing Frozen. Meteor." Aizen's biggest advantage is. that he eventually sided with the good. guys, only needing to show up at. specific moments to play the big shot. and carry the team. Everyone can just. laugh at that mustache-faced guy; especially in the latest episode, who. would’ve thought he’d use himself. as bait to successfully trick Yhwach. with Kyoka Suigetsu? That’s such a. cool development, making you love this. charismatic and imposing villain even. more. As for his backstory, I think. this is another area where Aizen is. quite well-written. As an emperor-type. figure, Aizen is actually positioned by. Kubo more as a rebel, a. revolutionary-type character; wasn't. the first step of his plan to secretly. purge the Central 46? Because to Aizen,. these high-ranking officials and noble. houses symbolized the corruption of the. Soul Society. Before losing to Ichigo. and being sealed by Urahara, Aizen even. questioned Urahara, "Do you really. intend to trust the rule of a thing. like that King?" And when you see the. secret of the Soul King revealed later. in the plot, you’ll think, "Oh, Aizen. was too extreme, but his approach. wasn't entirely without reason." I’m. sure you’ve all heard this old saying. , right? Truly great villains are the. heroes of their own stories. Aizen fits. this standard perfectly; he truly. believed that it would be better for. him to rule the three worlds than to. let these incompetent fools do it. Compared to him, Yhwach’s scope and. vision fall a bit short, I have to say. I personally don’t mind villains.

without grand ideals, whether it’s a. tragic backstory or a cowardly, petty. scumbag; to me, these are just. categories, and there’s no. superiority between them. There are. good petty villains among the petty. ones, right? And there are both. successful and failed cases for. emperor-style villains as well. A major. problem*Jujutsu Kaisen*is facing today. is that Gege-sensei seems to have. forgotten to come up with a motive for. Sukuna’s destructive actions. What is. his goal? What does he want to achieve? We honestly have no idea. He just got. resurrected one day for no reason, and. decided, "Alright, I'll just cause some. destruction and wipe out humanity then. " That’s it; as the main antagonist,. Sukuna remains incredibly hollow from. start to finish. As for his past. connections, miraculously, none of them. were ever given any real substance. Yorozu wanted to teach Sukuna about. love, but in the end, we learned. nothing about love; Angel said they’d. kill "The Fallen," and Sukuna admitted. he was "The Fallen," so what now? Who. knows. Also, Sukuna is clearly stated. to be the strongest of the ancient era,. so who exactly defeated him back then? It wasn't Ryu, and it wasn't Uraume, so. what gives? Did Yoriichi just happen to. pass by or something? Where did Gege. actually start adding some layers to. Sukuna? Right, after he got taken out. by Yuji. Sukuna admits that he didn't. really want to be an isolated King of. Curses; it was simply that as a " misfortune," he was rejected by the. world since birth, so he had to reject. the world in return. If he had another. life, he might have tried to live. differently. After watching this part. and looking back at the Arrancar Arc. and the interpretation of Aizen, I. realized Gege-sensei seems to have " borrowed" again. It's said that all one. could feel from Aizen’s spiritual. pressure was total loneliness; perhaps. he just wanted to be an ordinary Soul. Reaper at first, but because his. intellect and power were superior to. anyone else's, he never found anyone. who could understand him or share his. concerns about the world. Aizen’s ultimate ambition to become. the ruler of the world may have stemmed. from his disappointment with it. Right. Honestly, I don’t think the part. where Gege tried to give Sukuna some. humanity at the end was that bad;

it’s just that the story has. accumulated so many flaws that you can. no longer objectively judge a single. segment of the plot anymore, you know? Yes, and regarding Aizen, there’s one. more point I think is pretty cool that. I’d like to share: his backstory with. Shinji. For one, the fact that the page. numbering for that arc actually counted. backwards was honestly so stylish. Even. crazier, did you think this arc would. explain why Aizen turned evil? Nope. Even in his own backstory, Aizen. remains the mastermind villain. It’s. like he’s saying, "You dare ask me. for an origin story? The audacity!" Of. course, I don't think Kubo-sensei had. that much in mind when drawing this arc. . I suspect he just wanted to explain. how Shinji and the Visoreds ended up in. the real world. However, because later. hit series increasingly love giving. villains at least somewhat sympathetic. backstories, it indirectly makes a pure. , inexplicable evil like Aizen seem. more refreshing. To sum up, why is. Aizen greater than Sukuna? To put it. bluntly, Aizen was luckier—he. didn’t have to be the final boss all. the way to the end, sparing him from. the declining plot quality in the later. stages. Later on, he served as the " enemy of my enemy," acting as an ally,. which gave him plenty of chances to. shine and really rack up some. likability. Finally, I should say. something nice about Jujutsu Kaisen, so. nobody thinks I’m just here to bash. it. I do think Sukuna has some. advantages over Aizen. First off, his " Heian era" four-armed form; if you ask. me, it’s much cooler than Aizen’s. giant butterfly form. Right, you know. the Bleach rule: whenever an enemy. evolves into a monster, they’re. guaranteed to lose. We’re playing a. game of tactical combat here, and. you’re choosing to turn into a. monster? That’s basically suicide. The Shinjuku battle against Sukuna. certainly provided enough material to. sustain countless roast videos,. that’s for sure. But, and this is a. big but, the way Aizen was defeated at. the end of the Arrancar arc wasn't. actually that much better. Sorry, but. personally, I’ve never been a huge. fan of that. The method for beating a. boss at every stage is always pulling a. brand-new, broken power-up out of thin. air and then coming back to one-shot. them. Can we use a little bit of.

strategy, please? That’s about it. So. , what are your thoughts? Feel free to. leave a comment and discuss. I’m. Jinchuan Yi, and I’ll see you in the. next video. y.

作者進一步探討，藍染之所以能成為 Jump 史上最令人敬佩的反派之一，在於他的威脅性不僅來自斬魄刀鏡花水月的絕對催眠，更來自他深沉的心計與人性操弄。透過過去戲耍平子真子的經典橋段，藍染證明了自身的智謀始終凌駕於眾人之上。相較於僅靠作者旁白單方面強調「實力尚未用盡」，藍染這種將計謀、性格與能力完美融合的表現，才真正構建出一個令人信服且深具層次的高智商反派。

然而，宿儺在後期與五條悟的宿命決戰中，反派格調徹底崩盤。作者分析指出，宿儺本身斬擊術式單一，在無法突破無下限術式的情況下過度仰賴魔虛羅，喪失了身為頂點強者的從容；更嚴重的是，作者過度濫用束縛機制，使原本精巧的「等價交換」淪為推進劇情的便利工具，甚至以極其微小的代價換取逆轉戰局的空間斬。這類失衡的劇情邏輯暴露出能力體系過度膨脹卻無法圓滿自洽的問題，最終讓宿儺在讀者眼中淪為被劇情強行偏袒的笑柄。

"overpowered" aspect, their character. traits are the same; both are the type. of tyrannical figures with pride higher. than the heavens. They both have two. underlings: Aizen has Gin and Tosen,. while Sukuna has Uraume. Their way of. speaking is also identical: one says, " From this point on, I will stand in the. heavens," while the other says, " You’re just a brat born in an era. without me." anyway, it’s good that you didn’t. give me any examples. Much like Aizen when he. faced Ichigo, he truly displayed the. status and intensity one would expect. Take his first battle against Jogo, for. example. Not only did he deliberately. use Jogo’s specialty, fire-based. techniques, to clash head-on, but he. did it specifically to crush him on his. own home turf. And when Jogo unleashed. his ultimate move, he still had the. leisure to teleport to Kusakabe and. play "Red Light, Green Light" with them. —don't move until the meteor hits,. and if you don't move, I’ll spare. your lives. Switching to Aizen,. there’s definitely that classic scene. where he shuts off the protagonist’s. BGM, right? And in the Thousand-Year. Blood War, Aizen was tied to a chair. for most of the time, yet his. individual contribution still. completely crushed every single captain. of the Gotei 13. Alright, pardon me, a. quick digression—I really have to say. that this is more of an issue with the. writing of the Blood War arc itself; the performance of half the captains in. the 13 squads can only be described as. embarrassing. These so-called "I can. beat you with one hand tied behind my. back" tactics are very effective at. making the audience feel the sheer. presence of this Demon King. And. another very important point: do you. remember what Sukuna said to Jogo after. defeating him? He gave Jogo a heartfelt. compliment. I must emphasize that this. behavior is a crucial trait for. king-type characters like Sukuna or. Aizen; they cannot simply be arrogant. For those worthy opponents, they must. also show a certain level of respect. Only then will this overlord feel like. a leader with principles, and only then. will that kingly demeanor truly shine. through. Conversely, if you just act. arrogant from start to finish, the. audience will eventually see through. your act and realize, "Oh no, you’re. just a petty giant," just like the. later Sukuna. Precisely because of this. , why are the characters being watered. down? I’m hitting Sukuna—is that. for real? Don't worry, Sukuna,. they’re just jealous of you! Memes.

like these have emerged one after. another. Hey, the multi-functional,. curved-shaping Twister latest model E4. from the Overlord world’s Overlord BD. has arrived with a bang! When you hear the. name Aizen, what’s the first thing. that comes to mind? That's right,. illusions and his revolt within the. Soul Society. These represent the sheer. strength that Aizen possesses, leaving. a deep impression on the audience. Personally, my favorite part has always. been how he cleverly tricked Shinji in. the past, making him think, "Oh, I've. already figured out your trail.""Too. bad, little did he know those clues. were actually provided to him by yours.

truly!" It was precisely because Shinji. was so guarded against Aizen and kept. him at a distance that he ended up. being fooled by the simplest of tricks. In reality, the person who had been. following him for the past few weeks. was just a random passerby, and he. didn't even notice. This scene shows us. that Aizen's illusions aren't just. limited to his Zanpakuto's abilities,. but are actually multifaceted,. incorporating his own character and. schemes—all of which are part of his. trickery. To me, this is a much more. effective way to depict a boss than. constantly hyping up how strong they. are or claiming they haven't even used. their full power yet. You know what I. mean? Because we both know that the battle. between Sukuna and Gojo in the manga is. the main reason his reputation as a. villain was completely trashed. Including the laughable "jumping" tactics from Yuji and the others, you. can feel that Sukuna was coddled by. Gege the whole way, right up until his. obligatory defeat at the end. There are. many theories as to why Sukuna's. performance in the later stages was so. pathetic. Some say it's because. Sukuna’s base technique is just too. weak—he just slices things up. Vow" mechanic was completely abused. It. was supposed to be a genius patch Gege. came up with to fix the "exposition. disease" trope. In Bleach, characters. act like idiots by explaining their. trump cards to enemies, causing them to. lose; in Jujutsu, doing that actually. benefits you, giving yourself a buff—. wow, how creative. Binding Vow gradually evolved from a. cool "equivalent exchange" into a "get. out of jail free" card that the author. forces into the plot to explain why. things turned out this way. whenever Sukuna uses this move, he has. to point his fingers and chant. Wow,. good grief, that is such an insanely. heavy and pathetic price to pay. It's. about the same concept as me trading. you a bottle cap for the one million. dollars in your hand. Both of the. aforementioned deductions are correct,. but ultimately, I still think it comes. down to the author himself. He made the. manga's ability system unnecessarily. complicated, but didn't have the energy. or skill to organize the logic clearly,. which is why the finished product had. so many issues in the later stages of. Bleach. If you ask me, I have the exact. same problem, especially with Yhwach's. "The Almighty." Honestly, and I say. this with a clear conscience, I think. the level of nonsense is on par with " Dragon's Claw" or "Flowing Frozen. Meteor." Aizen's biggest advantage is. that he eventually sided with the good. guys, only needing to show up at. specific moments to play the big shot. and carry the team. Everyone can just. laugh at that mustache-faced guy; especially in the latest episode, who. would’ve thought he’d use himself. as bait to successfully trick Yhwach. with Kyoka Suigetsu? That’s such a. cool development, making you love this. charismatic and imposing villain even. more. As for his backstory, I think. this is another area where Aizen is. quite well-written. As an emperor-type. figure, Aizen is actually positioned by. Kubo more as a rebel, a. revolutionary-type character; wasn't. the first step of his plan to secretly. purge the Central 46? Because to Aizen,. these high-ranking officials and noble. houses symbolized the corruption of the. Soul Society. Before losing to Ichigo. and being sealed by Urahara, Aizen even. questioned Urahara, "Do you really. intend to trust the rule of a thing. like that King?" And when you see the. secret of the Soul King revealed later. in the plot, you’ll think, "Oh, Aizen. was too extreme, but his approach. wasn't entirely without reason." I’m. sure you’ve all heard this old saying. , right? Truly great villains are the. heroes of their own stories. Aizen fits. this standard perfectly; he truly. believed that it would be better for. him to rule the three worlds than to. let these incompetent fools do it. Compared to him, Yhwach’s scope and. vision fall a bit short, I have to say. I personally don’t mind villains.

without grand ideals, whether it’s a. tragic backstory or a cowardly, petty. scumbag; to me, these are just. categories, and there’s no. superiority between them. A major. problem*Jujutsu Kaisen*is facing today. is that Gege-sensei seems to have. forgotten to come up with a motive for. Sukuna’s destructive actions. What is. his goal? What does he want to achieve? We honestly have no idea. He just got. resurrected one day for no reason, and. decided, "Alright, I'll just cause some. destruction and wipe out humanity then. " That’s it; as the main antagonist,. Sukuna remains incredibly hollow from. start to finish. As for his past. connections, miraculously, none of them. were ever given any real substance. Yorozu wanted to teach Sukuna about. love, but in the end, we learned. nothing about love; Angel said they’d. kill "The Fallen," and Sukuna admitted. he was "The Fallen," so what now? Who. knows. Also, Sukuna is clearly stated. to be the strongest of the ancient era,. so who exactly defeated him back then? It wasn't Ryu, and it wasn't Uraume, so. what gives? Did Yoriichi just happen to. pass by or something? Where did Gege. actually start adding some layers to. Sukuna? Right, after he got taken out. by Yuji. Sukuna admits that he didn't. really want to be an isolated King of. Curses; it was simply that as a " misfortune," he was rejected by the. world since birth, so he had to reject. the world in return. If he had another. life, he might have tried to live. differently. After watching this part. and looking back at the Arrancar Arc. and the interpretation of Aizen, I. realized Gege-sensei seems to have " borrowed" again. It's said that all one. could feel from Aizen’s spiritual. pressure was total loneliness; perhaps. he just wanted to be an ordinary Soul. Reaper at first, but because his. intellect and power were superior to. anyone else's, he never found anyone. who could understand him or share his. concerns about the world. Aizen’s ultimate ambition to become. the ruler of the world may have stemmed. from his disappointment with it. Right. Honestly, I don’t think the part. where Gege tried to give Sukuna some. humanity at the end was that bad;

it’s just that the story has. accumulated so many flaws that you can. no longer objectively judge a single. segment of the plot anymore, you know? Yes, and regarding Aizen, there’s one. more point I think is pretty cool that. I’d like to share: his backstory with. Shinji. For one, the fact that the page. numbering for that arc actually counted. backwards was honestly so stylish. Even. crazier, did you think this arc would. explain why Aizen turned evil? Nope. Even in his own backstory, Aizen. remains the mastermind villain. It’s. like he’s saying, "You dare ask me. for an origin story? The audacity!" Of. course, I don't think Kubo-sensei had. that much in mind when drawing this arc. . I suspect he just wanted to explain. how Shinji and the Visoreds ended up in. the real world. However, because later. hit series increasingly love giving. villains at least somewhat sympathetic. backstories, it indirectly makes a pure. , inexplicable evil like Aizen seem. more refreshing. To sum up, why is. Aizen greater than Sukuna? To put it. bluntly, Aizen was luckier—he. didn’t have to be the final boss all. the way to the end, sparing him from. the declining plot quality in the later. stages. Later on, he served as the " enemy of my enemy," acting as an ally,. which gave him plenty of chances to. shine and really rack up some. likability. Right, you know. the Bleach rule: whenever an enemy. evolves into a monster, they’re. guaranteed to lose. We’re playing a. game of tactical combat here, and. you’re choosing to turn into a. monster? That’s basically suicide. The Shinjuku battle against Sukuna. certainly provided enough material to. sustain countless roast videos,. that’s for sure. But, and this is a. big but, the way Aizen was defeated at. the end of the Arrancar arc wasn't. actually that much better. Sorry, but. personally, I’ve never been a huge. fan of that. The method for beating a. boss at every stage is always pulling a. brand-new, broken power-up out of thin. air and then coming back to one-shot. them. Can we use a little bit of.

strategy, please? That’s about it. So. , what are your thoughts? Feel free to. leave a comment and discuss. I’m. Jinchuan Yi, and I’ll see you in the. next video. y.
